21:52 Local Time, 11:22 GMT, 16:52 IST: After getting thrashed in Perth, England roar back in style with a convincing 135-run win here in Adelaide. Inserted to bat, England posted their highest ODI total in Australia (355). Tom Banton compiled a beautiful century, three more English batters (Root, Cox and Jacks) scored fifties and there were cameos from Curran and Atkinson to power the visitors to an above-par total on a good batting deck.

Under lights, England's new-ball bowlers got the ball to move in the air and off the deck. They removed Australia's top four in 7 overs, reducing them to 29/4, with Atkinson taking three wickets. Things could have gone worse for the home team. Matt Renshaw and Cameron Green got reprieves, recorded fifties and forged a 98-run stand. But at no stage, did they put the England bowlers under any sort of pressure. The left-hander fell to Dawson, while attempting the reverse sweep against Dawson. Curran returned to remove Edwards and Bartlett off successive deliveries and then Green was stumped in a weird way in the very next over. Zampa, Johnson and Meredith got to double-digits, something that their top four couldn't achieve and managed to delay the inevitable.

Tom Banton | Player of the Match: [On playing at the Adelaide Oval and experiencing a memorable day] It's my first time in Adelaide. I've watched a lot of cricket in Australia over the years, the Ashes, white-ball series. So, to come here today is a pretty special feeling. [On his batting approach] 50-over cricket is hard. Sometimes you get off to a flyer and then you've got to rein it back in. And vice versa. So I think it's just picking moments and match-ups. The square boundaries here are a bit smaller than normal. So that was kind of my game plan, anything into the wicket, try and take that on. [On batting alongside Joe Root] Yeah, definitely. Played with Rootsy a little bit now, and to have him at the other end, he's such a calm head and makes it a lot easier for me. He's one of the greats of the game. To be able to stand at the other end and watch him go about his business is pretty cool. [On his bowling] I've been working on my bowling at the nets. But, it's a lot harder in a game.

The scoreline reads 1-1 going into the series decider. The action moves to Hobart. After two one-sided encounters, let's hope that we get a thriller on Wednesday (November 18th). For now, it's goodbye from all of us down here...
